name: cponfork_notes_check
prose: Precondition: kq is an open kqueue descriptor of a KQUEUE_CPONFORK queue and clofd the descriptor of another kqueue that was closed on fork; the parameters are not validated. Postcondition: it takes the expected-event mask from cponfork_notes_mask(true), which is RECV_TIMER | RECV_VNODE (0x03) because the parent-only RECV_CLOREAD bit is excluded in the child, registers a one-shot 4 second EVFILT_TIMER with ident TIMER_TIMEOUT and returns RECV_ERROR (0x80) if that kevent call fails. It then loops while the received bits do not cover the mask, waiting for one event at a time with kevent: a failing wait returns RECV_ERROR; a wait that returns 0 ends the loop; an EVFILT_TIMER event with ident TIMER_TIMEOUT returns the bits received so far ORed with RECV_ERROR; any other timer event sets RECV_TIMER; an EVFILT_VNODE event sets RECV_VNODE (its ident is not checked); an EVFILT_READ event whose ident is not clofd returns received ORed with RECV_ERROR, otherwise it sets RECV_CLOREAD; other filters are ignored. When the loop ends it returns the received bits, which include RECV_TIMER and RECV_VNODE and, if that event arrived before the loop ended, also RECV_CLOREAD (0x03 or 0x07), or fewer bits if the wait returned 0.
note: Read kqueue_fork.c:88-182 in full. Reviewers right: round 2 (the expected child mask is 0x03, not 0x07: cponfork_notes_mask(true) excludes the parent-only bit, 133-134); round 15 (0x83 cannot be returned: the loop ends once both RECV_TIMER and RECV_VNODE are set). Contract left empty because the function runs system calls on a kqueue.

name: test_kevent_vnode_disable_and_enable
prose: Precondition: the test globals are set: kqfd is a kqueue descriptor and vnode_fd an open descriptor on ./kqueue-test.tmp, and no kevent is pending on kqfd (the first test_no_kevents call checks this; its behaviour on a pending event was not read). Postcondition: it announces the test, checks there are no pending kevents, adds an EVFILT_VNODE watch for NOTE_ATTRIB on vnode_fd with EV_ADD | EV_ONESHOT and immediately disables it with EV_DISABLE, touches ./kqueue-test.tmp through system() and checks that no kevent is delivered, re-enables the watch with EV_ENABLE, touches the file again and waits (without a timeout) for one kevent, which must have ident vnode_fd, filter EVFILT_VNODE and fflags NOTE_ATTRIB. Any failing kevent call, a system() return below 0, a wait returning less than 1 event, or a wrong event calls err(1, ...), which prints a message and exits the process with status 1; on success it calls success() and returns.
note: Read vnode.c:222-261. Reviewers right: round 1 (the function adds the watch itself, 233-235), round 15 (the first test_no_kevents at 230 assumes no events pending).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(7_stress, dummy)
prose: Generated function 7_stress_body(dummy), produced by ATF_TC_BODY(7_stress, dummy). Takes the ATF test case pointer (unused) and returns void. It initializes a libalias instance (ATF_REQUIRE it is non-NULL), sets its address to masq, allocates an IP packet buffer with ip_packet(0, 64) (not checked) and a zeroed batch array of 1200 flows (ATF_REQUIRE non-NULL). For each of 25 rounds it fills every flow with a source and destination address taken from one of four fixed address pairs (selected by i & 3) with the low 16 bits randomized, and random ports between 1000 and 60000. It then runs UDP_NAT_CHECK for each flow, which sends the outbound packet through libalias and checks that the source becomes masq, records the alias port seen, shuffles the batch with qsort using randcmp, and runs UDP_UNNAT_CHECK for each flow, checking that the reply to the alias port is translated back to the original source address and port. The check macros report failures through ATF. After the rounds it frees the batch and the packet and calls LibAliasUninit.

name: fullsocket
prose: Precondition: none beyond the test harness; the function reads the global request header hdr (an RTM_GETLINK request). Postcondition: it creates a PF_NETLINK SOCK_RAW NETLINK_ROUTE socket and reads its SO_SNDBUF and SO_RCVBUF sizes (all required with ATF_REQUIRE), sends one request and uses a peeking MSG_WAITALL receive and FIONREAD to learn the size of one reply (rsize). It then loops sending the request with MSG_DONTWAIT without reading replies: a successful send increments a counter, a failed send must have errno EAGAIN and the bytes sent so far must exceed the send buffer size (both checked with ATF_REQUIRE); after each send it reads FIONREAD and FIONWRITE, and the loop continues while recvavail <= recvspace - rsize or sendavail <= sendspace - sizeof(hdr). It returns the descriptor when the loop ends. Any failing ATF_REQUIRE ends the test case, in which case the function does not return.
note: Slice cut the head; real function fullsocket (netlink_socket.c:72-117), read in full. Contract left empty: reviewer round 15 right that the old contract (result >= 0 only) omitted the flooding behaviour.

name: BITSTRING_TC_DEFINE(bit_set)
prose: Generated function bit_set_test(bitstr, nbits, memloc), whose definition head is produced by BITSTRING_TC_DEFINE(bit_set) (the same macro also defines the ATF test body that runs it through bitstring_test_runner). Precondition: bitstr points to a writable bitstring of at least bitstr_size(nbits) bytes (allocated on the stack or on the heap by bitstring_test_runner for nbits in {0, 1, _BITSTR_BITS-1, _BITSTR_BITS, _BITSTR_BITS+1, 2*_BITSTR_BITS-1, 2*_BITSTR_BITS, 1023, 1024}) and memloc is a string used only in failure messages. Postcondition: it clears the whole bitstring with memset, then for each i in 0..nbits-1 sets bit i, requires through ATF_REQUIRE_MSG for every j in 0..nbits-1 that the expression bit_test(bitstr, j) == (j == i) ? 1 : 0 is true, which, because == binds tighter than ?:, holds exactly when bit j is set if and only if j == i, and then clears bit i again. A failed requirement ends the test case. The function returns void and changes only *bitstr.

name: printblk
prose: Precondition: fs is a valid struct fs; the callers pass blocks in increasing logical block number order for ordinary blocks (lastlbn > 0), -level (<= 0) for indirect blocks and 0 for the final flush. The function keeps a run of blocks in static state (seq, totfrags, firstblk, lastblk, lastindirblk) across calls. Postcondition: returns nothing. With lastlbn > 0: if no run is active (seq == 0) it starts one from this block and returns without printing; if lbn == 0 it resets the static state (seq, totfrags, lastblk, firstblk, lastindirblk) to start a new run from this block and returns without printing the old run; if lbn < lastlbn and the block continues the run (both holes, both BLK_NOCOPY, both BLK_SNAP, or blkno equals firstblk + seq * fs_frag) it extends the run and returns. Otherwise (or when lastlbn <= 0) it flushes: if a run is active it prints one line for it, "lbn a[-b] hole|nocopy|snapblk" for sentinel runs or "lbn a[-b] blkno x[-y]" plus the distance from lastblk for real blocks (updating lastblk), where the run's last block number is derived from lbn; then, when lastlbn > 0 or blkno == 0, it starts a new run from the current block and returns. Otherwise it falls to the indirect-block print, which updates lastindirblk, prints "<level>-level indirect, blkno a-b" with the distance, updates lastindirblk (and lastblk when fs_metaspace is 0), and sets seq to 0.
note: Read prtblknos.c:224-302 in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (indirect calls pass lastlbn = -level and the function prints the indirect-level line, 295), round 15 (lastlbn is not simply the last lbn: here it also encodes level and the final flush); the prose avoids claiming its exact meaning. distance() and the callers were not read.

name: dowordfile
prose: Precondition: fname is a non-NULL NUL-terminated file name. Postcondition: it opens the file for reading and returns -1 if that fails (nrandwords and randwords unchanged). It sets nrandwords to the number of fgets calls with a 64-byte buffer needed to read the whole file (a line longer than 63 bytes is counted once per chunk, so this is not strictly the number of lines). It returns -1 after closing the file if ferror is set or rewinding with fseek fails (nrandwords then holds that count and randwords is unchanged), or if calloc of nrandwords pointers returns NULL. Otherwise it reads the file again with the same chunking, strips the first CR or LF and everything after it from each chunk (strcspn at the first occurrence, so not only a trailing newline) and stores a strdup copy in randwords[i]; a failed strdup calls err(1, ...) and exits the process. The second pass stops after the counted number of entries. It then sets nrandwords to that counted number (also if fewer were read, leaving the remaining entries NULL), closes the file and returns 0.
note: Read gaithrstress.c:149-182 in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (chunks of fgets are counted, long lines count several times, 159-160), round 15 (strcspn truncates at the first CR or LF, 169).

name: recv_loop_with_match
prose: Precondition: sock is a datagram socket, group and source point to sockaddrs, source is asserted to be AF_INET, and the global timeout is a number of seconds. Postcondition: returns 0 at once when timeout is 0. It resolves group and source to numeric host strings with getnameinfo and returns that call's nonzero error code (after printing it) if either fails. Otherwise it prints a waiting message, installs signal_handler for SIGINT and SIGALRM, sets an alarm of timeout seconds, and loops under setjmp calling recvfrom (its return value is not checked, and the address length argument is the uninitialized from.sa.sa_len); a datagram whose IPv4 source address equals the blocked source's address breaks out of the loop, any other datagram is counted. After the loop it reports the count when doverbose is set and sets the result from the setjmp value: SIGALRM gives 0, SIGINT prints "interrupted" and gives 20, a break out of the loop (value 0) prints a FAIL message and gives EX_IOERR, any other value prints a warning and gives EX_OSERR. It restores SIGINT and SIGALRM to SIG_DFL and returns the result.
note: Slice cut the head; real function recv_loop_with_match (ipmulticast.c:650-733), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (a getnameinfo error is returned before waiting), round 15 (recvfrom failure is never checked; EX_OSERR only arises from an unexpected longjmp value, 723-726).

name: test_fcntl
prose: Precondition: none; the function opens its own descriptors (it relies on /etc/passwd, a PF_LOCAL stream socket and SHM_ANON shared memory being available). Postcondition: it returns PASSED or FAILED (the success variable, which the REQUIRE, CHECK_* and FAIL macros, not read here, update). It opens the file, the socket and the shared-memory object, makes a capability for each with rights CAP_READ | CAP_FCNTL (cap_new), requires every descriptor to be valid, enters capability mode, and then for each of the six descriptors (the three raw ones and the three capabilities) requires fcntl(F_GETFL) to succeed, makes a new capability from it with only CAP_READ, and, provided a plain fcntl(F_GETFL) on the descriptor itself did not fail, checks that fcntl(F_GETFL) on the new CAP_READ-only capability fails with ENOTCAPABLE. None of the descriptors are closed before returning.
note: Read cap_test_fcntl.c:61-113. Reviewers right: round 2 (descriptors are never closed), round 15 (the CAP_READ|CAP_FCNTL capabilities are in the all[] array, so F_GETFL must succeed on them too, 87-91, 104). The behaviour of CHECK_SYSCALL_SUCCEEDS/CHECK_NOTCAPABLE/REQUIRE was not read.

name: main
prose: Precondition: none; main takes no arguments. Postcondition: if modfind("accf_data") returns -1 it prints "1..0 # SKIP ..." and calls _exit(0) without returning. Otherwise it prints "1..12" and runs the accept-filter steps on a loopback TCP socket bound to port 8080: socket, getsockopt(SO_ACCEPTFILTER) before and after bind (must fail with EINVAL), a setsockopt before listen (must fail), a getsockopt after that (EINVAL), listen, getsockopt before installing (EINVAL), setsockopt of the filter after listen (must succeed), getsockopt returning the filter name, a non-blocking accept sequence with a connected client (an accept before data must not succeed and after writing one byte must succeed), and a reset connection accepted with ECONNABORTED. It then leaves one connected socket on the incomplete queue, removes the accept filter with setsockopt(NULL, 0), requires a following getsockopt to fail with EINVAL, closes the listening socket, prints "ok 13 - setsockopt" and returns 0. Every failed check calls errx(-1, "not ok N ..."), which exits the process with status 255 and does not return. The printed plan says 12 but 13 ok lines are printed.
note: Slice cut the head and the tail; real function main (accf_data_attach.c:61-297), read in full. Reviewer round 15 is wrong for the real file: it does print "ok 13" and removes the filter (277-294); the reviewer saw only the cut slice ending at ok 12. Reviewer round 1/2 (the module-missing path exits 0 without returning) right.

name: main
prose: Precondition: argc and argv from the command line. Postcondition: if argc is not 2, or argv[1] converts with strtol (base 10) to a value outside 0..65535 or has trailing characters, it calls usage(), which prints a message and exits with errx(-1) (so main does not return); an empty argv[1] is accepted as port 0. It then runs the SIGPIPE tests: over PF_LOCAL stream socketpairs test_send_wantsignal and test_write_wantsignal, and, when SO_NOSIGPIPE is defined, test_send_dontsignal and test_write_dontsignal; a socketpair failure calls err(-1, ...) and exits. It then repeats the four tests (the don't-signal ones only with SO_NOSIGPIPE) over TCP socket pairs made with tcp_pair on the given port after tcp_setup(port), calls tcp_teardown(), prints "PASS" to stderr and returns 0. The test helper functions were not read.
note: Slice cut the head; real function main (sigpipe.c:249-320), read in full. Reviewer round 15 right: empty argv[1] gives port 0 and is accepted (258-259). usage() at 52-56 is errx(-1, ...).

name: bind_test
prose: Precondition: directory_path is a NUL-terminated directory name. Postcondition: returns 0 only after all steps succeed, otherwise -1 after printing a warning and closing the sockets it holds. It creates a PF_UNIX stream socket, composes directory_path "/" SOCK_NAME_ONE (-1 if it does not fit in PATH_MAX or sun_path), binds the socket to it, and records the path with push_path (which calls err(-1, ...) and exits the process when unwind_len is already UNWIND_MAX). It then requires a second bind of the same socket to fail with EINVAL, creates a second socket and requires its bind to the same path to fail with EADDRINUSE, closes the first socket and requires the second bind to still fail with EADDRINUSE, unlinks the path, binds the second socket to it successfully, closes it and returns 0. The socket file is left on disk (and in the unwind list) from the first successful bind on, so on the success path it exists again after the final bind and on later failures it may or may not exist.
note: Read unix_bindconnect.c:83-191 and push_path/unwind (61-80). Reviewers right: round 1 (push_path can exit instead of returning, 64-65), round 2 (after the unlink the final bind failure leaves no name; the name is not always left).

name: t_cmsg_len_client
prose: Precondition: fd is an open socket descriptor; the uc_cfg and sync infrastructure is initialized. Postcondition: it first calls uc_sync_recv and returns -2 at once if that fails (nothing is allocated yet). Otherwise it sets the result to -2, allocates CMSG_SPACE(sizeof(struct cmsgcred)) bytes and returns -2 (through the cleanup label) if malloc fails, initializes a message with one SCM_CREDS control message, and returns -2 if uc_socket_connect fails. It then sets the result to -1 and tries each cmsg_len from 0 up to CMSG_LEN(0) - 1 with sendmsg: a failing sendmsg continues with the next length, and the first successful sendmsg ends the loop. If all lengths failed (the loop reached CMSG_LEN(0)) the result becomes 0. It then calls uc_sync_send and returns -2 if that fails. The control buffer is freed on all paths after its allocation attempt, and the function returns the result (0 when all sends with a too-short cmsg_len failed, -1 when one succeeded).
note: Read t_cmsg_len.c:44-100. Reviewers right: round 1 (uc_socket_connect failure returns -2, 69-70), round 15 (the early uc_sync_recv return at 54-55 happens before cmsg_data is set, so nothing is freed there).

name: t_sockcred_1
prose: Precondition: the global uc_cfg harness state is initialized and the process may fork. Postcondition: it forks with uc_client_fork. In the child (case 0) it runs up to two client passes: each creates a socket (a failure gives -2), runs t_sockcred_client(1, fd), closes the socket (a failed close gives -2), and stops at the first nonzero result; the child then calls uc_client_exit with that result. In the parent (case 1) it creates a socket (a failure sets -2 and the child is not waited for), runs t_sockcred_server(1, fd) and, if that returned 0, t_sockcred_server(3, fd), then reaps the child with uc_client_wait; the result becomes the client's result when the server result is 0, or when it is -2 and the client result is nonzero (a server result of -1 is kept as -1), and a failed close of the socket sets -2. A fork failure returns -2. The function returns 0, -1 or -2 in the parent and, in the child, the call to uc_client_exit does not return (assumed from its name; not read).
note: Read t_sockcred.c:152-194. Reviewers right: round 1 (the child is not reaped when the parent socket creation fails, 175-177), round 2 (a server check failure returns -1 rather than -2, 179-184).

name: main
prose: Precondition: argc and argv are the command line. Postcondition: it parses options with getopt_long: --bufsize (strtonum in 1..UINT_MAX, errx(1) if it fails or is not a power of two), --cons-type (mc, mc-mt, sc, peek or peek-clear, else errx(1)), --prod-count (strtonum in 1..UINT_MAX, errx(1) on error), and help or an unknown option calls usage(). It exits with errx(1) when no consumer type or no producer count was given. If no size was given the buffer size is next_power_of_2(prod_count). For the mc-mt consumer it allocates the mt_seen array with calloc without checking it. It then allocates the ring with buf_ring_alloc (not checked), starts one consumer thread (two for mc-mt) and prod_count producer threads (allocated with calloc, asserted non-NULL), each pthread_create checked with assert, joins all producers and the consumers with assert on each result, prints the expected count PROD_ITERATIONS * prod_count and the total consumed count, frees the ring and returns 0. The asserts are compiled out when NDEBUG is defined.
note: Slice cut the head; real function main (buf_ring_test.c:219-322), read in full. Reviewer round 15 right: the mt_seen calloc (284-285) and buf_ring_alloc (288) are not checked. The getopt string "bf:" lists only b and f, while the switch handles b, c, p and h through longopts; that mismatch is not analysed here.
